samples.summary: New third structural-op guard in `resolveNode` has no counterpart in the client mirror contract (`SceneNodeMeta.structuralEditable`) or the engine spec, which both describe exactly TWO guards
samples.evidence: `packages/design-editor/src/types.ts:115-116` documents `structuralEditable` as "Mirrored server-side as a hard guard in `resolveNode`", and `docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-engine.md:754-766` states "**Two structural-op guards, both server-side** (`requireStatic`)" — scope-must-be-static and node-must-be-a-direct-JSX-child. The implementation adds a third, undocumented refusal: `isReturnsRoot(root) && root.jsx.includes(hit.node)` refuses every top-level returned element (packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs, `resolveNode`). Any extractor/UI computing `structuralEditable` from the documented two-guard rule (the only rule written down today) will mark the root element of every single-return component as structurally editable, and every such edit will be refused server-side. jsx-nodes.mjs exports no shared predicate for the three-part rule, so the mirror must reimplement it — precisely the drift the module's header says must never happen. Fix belongs on the new code: export a `structuralEditableOf(entry, root)` helper and update the spec + `SceneNodeMeta` doc.

verdict.reason: The factual evidence checks out: the third refusal exists at packages/design-editor/src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs:765-773, types.ts:115-116 calls structuralEditable a server-mirrored guard, and design-editor-engine.md:754-766 says "Two structural-op guards". But the blocking impact rests on a consumer that does not exist in this repository. Repo-wide grep for `structuralEditable` returns exactly two hits: the declaration at packages/design-editor/src/types.ts:116 and a shape fixture at packages/design-editor/test/types.test.ts:31. Nothing computes it. The extractor named in the types.ts header (scripts/extract-design-metadata.mjs) is absent; the entire package is four files (src/server/jsx-nodes.mjs, src/types.ts, and two tests) with no extract.mjs, inject.mjs, or UI, and grep for design-metadata/SceneNodeMeta outside the package hits only design docs and package manifests. The only actual callers of resolveNode are the package tests, which already assert the third guard (test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs:259-263 refuses a top-level returned element; :280-281 keeps attribute edits allowed). So there is no broken caller, no bypassing entry point, and no code site that needs to change. What is left is a spec paragraph and a type doc-comment describing the older two-guard contract — which this lens's own severity table classifies as minor ("a type, doc, or comment left describing the old contract"), and spec fit is explicitly deferred to the design-fit lens. Real drift, but not blocking under the blast-radius rubric.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is factually correct (no esModuleInterop/allowSyntheticDefaultImports in packages/design-editor/tsconfig.json; allowJs:true at line 44; include covers src so the @ts-check'd jsx-nodes.mjs is now checked; it default-imports the `export = ts` typescript module at line 21). But the predicted failure is a counterexample: TS1259 is gated on `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`, whose documented default is true when esModuleInterop is on OR module is `system` OR moduleResolution is `bundler`. This tsconfig sets "moduleResolution": "bundler" (line 19) with "module": "ESNext" (line 18), so synthetic default imports are implicitly enabled and `import ts from 'typescript'` type-checks; the checker resolves such a default to the module symbol, so the JSDoc `ts.Node` type references (e.g. line 35) resolve too. Bundler resolution also does not set impliedNodeFormat, so the node16/nodenext ESM→CJS default-import restrictions do not apply to the .mjs file. The cited contrast file packages/cli/tsconfig.json sets esModuleInterop (line 10) but also uses moduleResolution bundler (line 5), so it does not demonstrate that the omission is load-bearing. node_modules is absent so tsc could not be executed, but the behaviour has been stable since TS 5.0 and the package pins typescript ^5.9.3 (package.json:13), so the enforced `typecheck` lane (package.json:8, `tsc --noEmit`) does not break for the stated reason.
